findings.evidence: CBG-003 removes automatic private governance PR/main builds, while CBG-014 relies on a local pre-push hook and CBG-018 forbids weakening or bypassing gates. Local hooks and local JSON evidence do not cover uninstalled hooks, --no-verify, alternate clones, GitHub web/API writes, or stale hook distribution, so AC-CBG-002 and AC-CBG-007 cannot prove a fail-closed fleet boundary.
findings.reevaluationTrigger: Re-review after the intake defines and tests an enforceable trust boundary, including hook installation/freshness and server-side or explicitly bounded equivalent protection for every push path.

findings.evidence: The target state and result artifacts require workflow-trigger, schedule, hook, and profile convergence across 48 repositories. The declared delivery authority is LocalImplementation, the Autonomous prompt permits only repository-owned changes, and the hard stops prohibit remote delivery. No separately governed rollout or acceptance handoff explains how fleet-wide AC-CBG-001 through AC-CBG-009 become true under that authority.
findings.reevaluationTrigger: Re-review after the intake splits Level-0 canonical implementation from a separately authorized fleet rollout, or otherwise aligns delivery authority, repositories in scope, handoff evidence, and stage-specific acceptance.

findings.evidence: CBG-001 says repository visibility and membership must be live-revalidated and are not timeless, while CBG-002 fixes the five profile cardinalities at 3/6/6/21/12 for exactly 48 repositories. The live snapshot currently matches 27 private and 21 public repositories, but the intake does not define deterministic classification rules or the required stop/update behavior when membership, visibility, or cardinality changes.
findings.reevaluationTrigger: Re-review after the intake defines repository-to-profile decision rules, canonical mapping evidence, and fail-closed behavior for fleet or visibility drift.
